name: alter self
lore:
# On the Transmutation of the Mortal Frame: Alter Self

To cast *Alter Self* is to treat the body as sculptor’s clay. As you draw upon the Weave, it feels less like a thread and more like a warm, viscous resin coating your spirit. The sensation is one of profound internal "restlessness"—a prickling heat in the marrow as your skeletal structure softens and reforms.

Visually, the transformation is a blur of kinetic potential. Observers see your skin ripple like a pond struck by heavy rain, features melting and re-knitting in a heartbeat. It is a violent grace; one moment a man, the next, a creature of scale and claw.

Legend attributes this art to the Archmage Valerius the Vain. Seeking to woo a moon-spirit who only loved the reflection of stars, Valerius spent decades distilling the essence of the mimic and the doppelgänger. He eventually succeeded, shedding his humanity to become whatever his beloved desired, though some say he eventually forgot his true face entirely.

Take heed, traveler: to change the vessel is to risk the contents. Hold fast to your soul, lest it slip through your new fingers.
